reason: method1 returns true when the two objects are equal according to their equals() method, regardless of class. method2 first checks that the two objects are of the same class; if they are not, it returns false even if equals() would return true. Using a java.util.Date and a java.sql.Date that represent the same instant demonstrates this difference: Date.equals(java.sql.Date) returns true, but the class check in method2 causes it to return false.
